第二屆全港青年辯論比賽冠軍
本校的同學素來熬中於辯論，中文學會爲
更進一步加强今年校際辯論實力，早
於去年八月已成立了校際中文辯論隊，並參加

出代表選手四名：馮敬德、馮志榮、廖志豪及

備時間只得五天，三名賽員日以繼夜，埋頭苦
幹，將全部時間、精神、心思花下去，不停開
會，檢討及改進，連反駁對手的駁詞亦一一準
備，可謂準備充足。幸而各人都懷着不論勝負

唇槍舌劍，香港華仁終以一千四百三十六分

這次參賽各小組都不是苟且，大體言之，鎏
賽各同學都有相當儀表，雄辯口才，敏捷
飽機智，尤其有一定學識和充分準備；特
別是冠軍隊在這些 條件表 現得最全面，最突

119.t: Mr. Wong Tuen Po, Robert
Robert Wong Tuen Po was quite
young
when he first left his
native Toi Shan dlistrict to come to
Hong Kong to study in St Joseph's
College. With school and Tteacher
training completed it was. not long be-
fore he joined Mr. Peter Tsui in Jan.
1922 in the recently founded Wah Yan
College.
It had shortly before moved
from Hollywood Road to Robinson
Road. As soon as room for a hostel
could be found, one was opened, espe-
cially for overseas boys.
Mr Wong
was the obvious one to manage it, for
no one else could ever think of looking
atter such a mixed group - some from
the interior of China some from Indo
China, as it was then called, many
from Siam and a number from all
parts of New Guinea. When in 1933
we Jesuit Fathers took over the running of Wah
Yan, we were fortunate that Mr. Wong remained on
the staff and gave us the full benefit of his know-
Iedge and experience. His pupils were fortunate to
have such a dedicated teacher.
AlsO, the fall of Hong Kong at Christmas 1941
Shattered our small world and early 1942 saw our
pupils, teachers and their families join the throngs
of refugees streaming into China along its roads and
rivers The aim of all of us refugees was simple -
‘survival util the end of the war.' Robert Wong
hike the rest turned his hand to many different jobs.
He taught school, interpreted for the Allied forces.
He took up contracting and dhid very well indeed.
During one period a group of Hong Kong Catholics
met at the South Church in Kweiyang city for
Sunday Mass. 1 attended one of these Masses with
Mr. Wong and.so met a group of Hong Kong folk.
Peace, though long in coming, came at last and
soon the human tide began to fow in the opposite
dlirection. Mr. Wong went back to his home and
family in Canton. He became a teacherin the
Catholic school there. In 1948 he was helping the
Hong Kong Jesuits who: were planning to start a
Middle School in Canton city. What a task we gave
him！- looking for a piece of land, and persuading
the owners to part. with it at a reasonable price！
1949 came and Canton and our hopes of new schools
went behind the Bamboo Curtain. Back we went
to/ Hong Kong, started an afternoon extension to
Wah Yan in Robinson Road: Again in 1952
another move was needed. The P.Ml. school was
closed and the new WWah Yan Kowloon wasto
receive the P.M. boys. Again Mr. Wong was a key
man in these new ventures. He remained actively
teaching in Wah Yan Kowloon until 1960, when he
retired.In 1977 in spite of the best possible medical
care and the great sacrifices made by his family the
original improvement was not maintained and death
came to him at the age of 79. The hospital chaplain
who had given him the Sacrament of the Sick was
Fr Casey a friend since early days in Wah Yan.
His old pupils will ever be grateful for his good
teaching but Hike all of us, they are still more in his
dlebt for the example he gave us of such a good life.
We can say with the prophet Malachy： “The instruc-
tion he gave was true and no harmful word ever
fell from his lips; he walked in harmony with me
and in purity of life.”
